holidays.name: National Milk Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating the smooth, creamy, sweet cousin of dark chocolate. Fans are encouraged to unwrap a milk chocolate bar, bake with it, or dunk anything within reach into a melted pool of it.
holidays.origin: A U.S. food holiday of unclear authorship, one of several chocolate days on the calendar. Milk chocolate itself was invented in 1875 in Switzerland by Daniel Peter, who teamed up with Henri Nestlé, the maker of condensed milk.
holidays.funFact: Daniel Peter spent about eight years perfecting his recipe because the water content in fresh milk kept ruining the chocolate. Condensed milk finally solved the problem.

holidays.name: National Hamburger Day (Alternate Observance: National Milk Chocolate Day's Neighbor) - World Hepatitis Day
holidays.description: A serious but important global awareness day dedicated to educating people about viral hepatitis, encouraging testing, vaccination, and treatment around the world.
holidays.origin: Observed on July 28 to honor the birthday of Nobel Prize winner Dr. Baruch Blumberg, who discovered the hepatitis B virus. The World Health Assembly officially designated it a World Health Organization day in 2010.
holidays.funFact: World Hepatitis Day is one of only eleven official global public health campaigns marked by the WHO. Blumberg also developed the first hepatitis B vaccine.

holidays.name: National Heavenly Hash Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the dessert delight known as heavenly hash, a sweet mix of chocolate, marshmallows, and nuts, often found in ice cream or candy form. Participants are encouraged to indulge in the gooey, crunchy, chocolatey combination.
holidays.origin: A foodie observance from the American snack calendar, rooted in Southern dessert traditions where the name 'heavenly hash' described a mix of fruit, marshmallows, and cream long before it became a rocky road cousin.
holidays.funFact: Heavenly hash has been the name of several different recipes, from a fruit salad with marshmallows to a chocolate candy, so nobody can agree what it actually is.

holidays.name: National Parents' Day (Fourth Sunday Cousin) / Rainbow Day Alternative: World Nature Conservation Day
holidays.description: A day to think about the planet's natural resources, from forests to rivers, and to take small steps like planting trees, picking up litter, or simply hugging a tree with no shame whatsoever.
holidays.origin: Observed internationally on July 28 as a way to promote the protection of natural resources, which are the foundation of a healthy society and a stable environment.
holidays.funFact: Trees in a forest can share nutrients and warning signals through underground fungal networks, which scientists have nicknamed the 'wood wide web.'

holidays.name: Beatrix Potter's Birthday
holidays.description: A cozy fan celebration of the English author and illustrator behind Peter Rabbit, with readers picking up a little book, wearing a blue jacket, or avoiding Mr. McGregor's garden.
holidays.origin: Helen Beatrix Potter was born on July 28, 1866, in London. Her books began as an illustrated letter to a sick child in 1893 and were self-published in 1901 after publishers rejected them.
holidays.funFact: Potter became a prize-winning sheep breeder and left more than 4,000 acres of land to Britain's National Trust, protecting the Lake District landscape.
